name: Molson Coors Beverage Company
one_line_reason: Fewer people drink mainstream American beer every year, the 2023 Bud Light windfall has worn off, and Molson Coors has now cut its 2026 profit guidance as volume falls faster than price can cover.
evidence: Q3 2026 brand volume fell 4.9% (Americas -5.3%) and financial volume fell 3.0%, with price/mix of only +1.8%; underlying pre-tax income fell 17.4% in constant currency (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-05). Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to net sales -1% to -2% and underlying pre-tax income -21% to -24% (previously -15% to -18%), after a $3.65B goodwill impairment on the Americas unit in Q3 2025 that already admitted the business is worth less. Net debt is $5.39B, 2.53x underlying EBITDA at 2026-09-30 versus 2.28x a year earlier.
key_numbers: P/FCF 7.1 vs 8.5 10y median; fwd P/E 9.3; FCF yield 14% (FY2025 FCF $1.07B); 9M26 brand volume -4.3%; net debt/EBITDA 2.53x; short interest 20.4%

name: Celsius Holdings, Inc.
one_line_reason: The flagship CELSIUS brand is shrinking and losing share, growth now comes only from the bought-in Alani Nu brand, and margins are falling, so the 2023 growth multiple has been taken away for good reason.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue rose 16.8% to $847.2M, but CELSIUS brand revenue fell about 6% to $356.8M and its US retail sales fell 7.0%, while Alani Nu (acquired 2025) rose 24% to $410.1M and Rockstar retail sales fell 13.2% (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-05). Gross margin fell 450 bps to 46.8% and adjusted EBITDA fell 3% to $198.6M; adjusted EPS was $0.41 vs $0.42 despite the acquisition-driven revenue jump. The diluted share count is up 14% over five years and 3y restructuring charges equal 13% of revenue (mostly the cost of ending distribution contracts on the move into PepsiCo's system).
key_numbers: P/E 76 vs 82 10y median; fwd P/E 19.6; P/FCF 25; FCF yield 3.9%; CELSIUS brand revenue -6% Q3 26; GM 46.8% (-450 bps); -66% from 3y high

name: Brown-Forman Corporation
one_line_reason: Developed-market drinkers are buying less American whiskey and tequila, sales have not grown in three years, and the recent jump in free cash flow comes mostly from laying down less whiskey, which is the company itself betting on lower future demand.
evidence: Q1 FY27 (quarter to 2026-07-31) net sales fell 1% (organic -1%) to $911M, with tequila -13% organic, Herradura -18%, Developed International -8% organic, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey flat; FY27 guidance is organic sales about flat and organic operating income down 3% to 5% (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-09-02). Revenue has fallen from $4.23B in FY2022 to $3.93B in FY2026 (3y CAGR -2.4%) and EPS has shrunk 4% a year over five years. Cash spent building inventory fell from $403M in FY2023 to $22M in FY2026 (10-K filed 2026-06-12), which explains most of the rise in operating cash flow from $0.60B to $1.00B.
key_numbers: P/E 19.7 vs 29.2 10y median; P/FCF 15.8 vs 40 (FCF flattered by inventory cut); FCF yield 6.3%; rev 3y CAGR -2.4%; FY27 organic op income guide -3% to -5%; -45% from 3y high

name: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.
one_line_reason: The stock is held down by a China-education discount plus two fixable bruises, a slowdown in overseas-study demand under US visa policy and margin dilution from the low-margin East Buy e-commerce arm, while the core education business keeps growing above 20% with a large cash pile.
evidence: Q1 FY27 (quarter to 2026-08-31) revenue rose 23.1% to $1,874.5M and operating income rose 20.5% to $374.7M, but operating margin slipped to 20.0% from 20.4% as East Buy grew; overseas test prep and consulting grew only 7.7% while domestic adult test prep grew 22.3% and new education initiatives 24.7% (EX-99.1, 6-K filed 2026-10-28). Deferred revenue, which is cash prepaid by students, was $2,121.1M, up 11.2% year on year, and FY27 revenue guidance of +14% to +18% was confirmed. The company held $1,754.6M cash, $1,441.3M term deposits and $2,422.7M short-term investments ($5.62B total) and has committed about $300M of dividends plus a $200M buyback for FY27.
key_numbers: P/E 17.3 (10y median meaningless after 2021 losses); fwd P/E 10.7; FCF yield 9.5%; cash+deposits+STI $5.62B vs mcap $8.22B; deferred revenue +11.2%; FY27 rev guide +14-18%; ~6% cash return yield; -43% from 3y high

name: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company
one_line_reason: The crush-margin slump and the 2024 accounting scandal that knocked ADM down are already reversing in public view, and at about 12x this year's raised earnings guidance the stock sits at its normal multiple, while the screen's 13% free-cash-flow yield is inflated by a one-year inventory release.
evidence: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.77 vs $0.92 and total segment operating profit rose 64% to $1,382M, led by Crushing (+$298M) on the EPA renewable-fuel volume rule finalized in March 2026; 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.50-$5.80 from $5.15-$5.60 (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-03). FY2025 operating cash flow of $5.45B included a $1.51B release from lower inventory values (10-K filed 2026-02-17), so the $4.20B FCF is not a run rate. The November 2024 Item 4.02 non-reliance filing on Nutrition segment reporting is two years old and the stock is up 15% over the last year.
key_numbers: price $67.78 = ~12x 2026 adj EPS guide midpoint $5.65 vs 12.6 10y median P/E; trailing GAAP P/E 30 on trough FY2025; FCF yield 13% incl. $1.5B inventory release; net debt $8.0B; shares -14% in 3y

name: Lamb Weston Holdings, Inc.
one_line_reason: The 2022-23 french-fry shortage that gave Lamb Weston pricing power is over, the industry has overbuilt capacity, and the company is now buying volume with price cuts, so profits have reset lower and the stock is not even cheap on the reset earnings.
evidence: FY2026 (to 2026-05-31) price/mix fell 6% while volume rose 7%, adjusted EBITDA was $1,147M against roughly $1.4B+ at the FY2024 peak, and Q4 International segment EBITDA fell 81% (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-07-24). Q1 FY27 price/mix fell another 2%, International sales fell 8% with segment EBITDA down 54% to $27M, and the company closed its Broekhuizenvorst plant; FY27 guidance is adjusted EBITDA of $1.125-$1.215B (flat) and adjusted EPS $3.05-$3.35 (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-10-06). Operating margin is 8.9% against a 10-year median of 15.5%.
key_numbers: ~16x FY27 adj EPS guide midpoint $3.20; EV/EBITDA ~9.3x; EV/EBIT 18.4 vs 17.2 10y median; P/E 24.8 vs 19.7; FCF yield 7.5%; FY26 price/mix -6%; net debt $3.7B; -49% from 3y high

name: General Mills, Inc.
one_line_reason: Americans are buying fewer boxes of cereal, snacks and packaged meals, General Mills had to cut prices to slow the volume loss, and earnings per share are guided down a third from the 2024 peak, so the low multiple is following falling profits rather than running ahead of them.
evidence: Q1 FY27 (to 2026-08-30) organic net sales were flat, North America Retail organic sales fell 3% with Big G cereal down double digits including the yogurt sale, adjusted operating profit fell 11% in constant currency and adjusted EPS fell 13% to $0.75 (EX-99, 8-K filed 2026-09-23). FY27 guidance: organic net sales -1.5% to +0.5%, adjusted operating profit -8% to -13%, adjusted EPS $3.00-$3.20, after FY2026 'base price investment actions' (price cuts) and $1.62B of impairments over three years; the company itself lists 'weight loss trends' as a demand risk. Buybacks stopped (none in Q1 FY27 vs $500M a year earlier) and net debt is $12.1B.
key_numbers: ~11x FY27 adj EPS guide $3.10 midpoint vs 13.6 10y median P/E; fwd P/E 11.0; P/FCF 11.4 vs 12.3; dividend yield ~7%; net debt $12.1B; FY27 adj op profit -8 to -13%; -48% from 3y high
